Validation results · synthetic sample — not a measurement

This page uses synthetic rows to illustrate the validation-page layout and deviation definition. They are not recorded runs, measurements or evidence about NSATS’s arrangement. Positions are relative to each sample’s start point, identified only by its gps_loc_code.

In engineering, validation examines whether a defined requirement is met in its intended use. A successful individual action can be one observation within that assessment, while the requirement may concern behaviour across the task.

Synthetic sample — not a measurement: Last addition: run G-SAMPLE-L18

How to read a run

Read the “Synthetic sample” label and start time with the sample’s setting. The synthetic reference and eight sensor paths illustrate how to read a run. The table contains synthetic field values in the before and after columns for NSATS’s proprietary noise filtering, together with synthetic calculated positions; these are not sensor measurements.

At each point the arrangement calculates a position afresh. Deviation is the horizontal distance between the calculated position and the reference position at that point. As a percentage, it is that distance divided by the distance moved since the previous point, multiplied by 100. The start point has no previous point and is excluded.

Range across synthetic samples — not a measurement

Synthetic sample — not a measurement: In 24 runs (cases: airborne at 100 km/h; airborne at 250 km/h; lab run at 1 m/s; land vehicle at 10 km/h; vessel at 10 knots; vessel at 20 knots; vessel at 5 knots), deviations ranged from 2.0 % to 12.0 % (0.04 to 262.38 m) under the settings listed.

Settings listed: airborne, laboratory, open country, open water.

Geomagnetism is currently offered under NSATS’s regular software licence agreement; further licence forms follow further validation.
